description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:1136-1143 — has_key_cert_sign uses .ok() to discard parse errors:
  `.and_then(|ext| KeyUsage::from_der(ext.extn_value.as_bytes()).ok())`
  `.map(|ku| ku.key_cert_sign())`

If the KeyUsage extension is structurally present but DER-malformed, from_der() returns Err, which .ok() converts to None. The function then returns None (meaning 'KeyUsage absent' → no constraint). 

For intermediate CA certificates, this means a malformed critical KeyUsage extension is treated as absent rather than causing a MalformedCertificate error. A critical extension that cannot be parsed MUST cause rejection per RFC 5280 §4.2.

The critical extension guard (check_critical_extensions at line 1019-1026) runs separately and checks whether the OID is in HANDLED_CRITICAL_OIDS. OID_KEY_USAGE is in that list (line 1007), so a malformed critical KeyUsage passes the critical extension check. Then has_key_cert_sign silently treats it as absent, skipping the keyCertSign enforcement.

Suggested fix: use try_find_cert_ext for KeyUsage in the CA-only check at line 2291, propagating parse errors as MalformedCertificate. The function has_key_cert_sign is inherently fail-open and should be replaced with a fail-closed variant in the CA-only check path.

P1 — a malformed critical KeyUsage on an intermediate CA silently passes keyCertSign enforcement.
title: has_key_cert_sign silently discards DER decode errors — malformed KeyUsage treated as absent
